agents.label: Design QA
agents.summary: The Corporate Counsel & Compliance Exchange USA microsite communicates the essential event information and has a reasonable structural skeleton, but suffers from consistent brand misalignment (Raleway instead of Archivo/Inter, blue/yellow instead of #0A2540/#FF5A36), unrefined spacing rhythm, and several mobile stacking issues that would be visible to any professional reviewer. The hierarchy works at a macro level but the registration CTA competes with secondary actions and the overall finish reads as a template-default rather than a deliberate design decision.

findings.location: Layout & grid · Key Themes section, desktop
findings.issue: The four theme cards appear to use a 4-column layout but the chess-board imagery bleeds into a dark background that creates an uncontrolled full-bleed zone; card edges do not align to the same horizontal baseline as the surrounding content columns, breaking grid continuity.
findings.recommendation: Constrain all card content to the same max-width container (e.g. 1200px) used by all other sections, and ensure card bottom-edges align on the same row baseline.
findings.fix_prompt: In the Key Themes section, wrap all four theme cards in a container with max-width: 1200px; margin: 0 auto; and set each card to the same min-height so their bottom edges align. Remove any negative margin or full-bleed class applied only to this section.

findings.issue: Only one speaker card is visible in the speakers row before the 'View all speakers' button, leaving the row mostly empty and creating a large unexplained void on the right side.
findings.recommendation: Show at least 4–6 speaker cards in a grid before the CTA, or explicitly communicate 'Featuring our first announced speaker' to avoid the appearance of broken content.
findings.fix_prompt: In the speakers section, change the speaker grid to display a minimum of 4 placeholder/confirmed speaker cards in a 4-column CSS grid (grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr)) before showing the 'View all speakers' CTA button.

findings.issue: Sponsor logos are arranged in uneven rows with varying vertical gaps; the last row has 3 logos left-aligned while all other rows are center-aligned, creating a ragged bottom edge.
findings.recommendation: Use a CSS flexbox row with justify-content: center and a consistent gap value so all rows center-align regardless of count.
findings.fix_prompt: Set the sponsor logo container to display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: center; align-items: center; gap: 24px; and ensure each logo item has a consistent width of 120px so rows balance visually.

findings.issue: The page uses Raleway as both primary and secondary font (confirmed in CSS: --primary-font and --secondary-font are both 'Raleway'). The brand configuration requires Archivo for headings and Inter for body text. This is a complete brand typography mismatch.
findings.recommendation: Replace the font imports and CSS variables to use Archivo for all headings and Inter for all body text, per brand config.
findings.fix_prompt: In the <style data-dynamic> block, replace the @import with @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Archivo:wght@400;600;700;800&family=Inter:wght@400;500;600&display=swap'); then update --primary-font to 'Archivo', sans-serif and --secondary-font to 'Inter', sans-serif.

findings.issue: The large numerals appear at an arbitrary size that is not in the brand type scale (12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48, 64px); they appear to be ~40px, sitting between defined scale steps.
findings.recommendation: Set stat numerals to exactly 48px (next scale step up) or 32px, and labels to 14px, both from the defined scale.
findings.fix_prompt: Find the statistics counter elements and set the numeral font-size to 48px and font-weight to 800 (Archivo), and the descriptor label below to font-size: 14px; font-weight: 400 (Inter).

findings.issue: The tagline 'Checkmate, Chaos – Turning Volatility Into Your Next Strategic Advantage' appears in a size between the h1 and h2, suggesting an intermediate heading level that is not part of the defined scale, and the line-height appears tight for a multi-line display headline.
findings.recommendation: Set the tagline to 32px (scale step) with line-height: 1.25 for display use, or promote to h2 at 48px with adequate line-height.
findings.fix_prompt: Set the hero tagline element's CSS to font-size: 32px; line-height: 1.25; font-family: 'Archivo', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; to align with the brand type scale.

findings.location: Typography · Body copy paragraphs, multiple sections (About section, Sponsorship section)
findings.issue: Body text line length on desktop appears to exceed 90 characters per line in full-width sections, reducing readability.
findings.recommendation: Cap body text containers at max-width: 720px or use a narrower column within the grid for prose content.
findings.fix_prompt: Add max-width: 720px; margin: 0 auto; to all body paragraph containers inside full-width section backgrounds to keep line length within the 45–90 character range.

findings.location: Spacing & rhythm · Between 'Key Themes' and 'Secure Your Place' CTA strip, desktop
findings.issue: The dark themed-cards section transitions immediately into the CTA strip with no visible vertical breathing room; the two sections appear merged, reducing scanability.
findings.recommendation: Add 48px top/bottom padding to the CTA strip to create a clear visual break between the sections.
findings.fix_prompt: Add padding-top: 48px; padding-bottom: 48px; to the .secure-your-place or equivalent CTA strip section class to create separation from the Key Themes cards above.

findings.location: Spacing & rhythm · Benefits of Attending / Benefits of Sponsoring tabs, desktop
findings.issue: The section heading 'Benefits of Attending' and 'Benefits of Sponsoring' have no visible content below them in the screenshot — the region appears empty with a large void below the tab labels before the next section begins.
findings.recommendation: Verify content is rendering inside the tabs. If content exists but is hidden, ensure the active tab has sufficient padding (min 48px) so the section does not look broken.
findings.fix_prompt: Inspect the Benefits tabs section; ensure the active tab panel has padding: 32px 0; and that its child content elements are not hidden by a CSS display:none or zero-height collapse. Add min-height: 200px to the tab panel container as a safeguard.

findings.issue: The four stat blocks have inconsistent horizontal gutters — the gaps between blocks appear wider between the 2nd and 3rd items than between the 1st and 2nd, suggesting margin rather than gap-based spacing.
findings.recommendation: Use CSS gap on a flexbox or grid container to ensure equal spacing between all stat blocks.
findings.fix_prompt: Wrap the four statistic blocks in a flex container with display: flex; justify-content: center; gap: 48px; and remove any individual margin-left or margin-right from the stat items.

findings.issue: Two CTA buttons are present in the hero ('Request Your Invite' and 'Explore Our Networking Event Format') at visually equal weight and similar size. The secondary action competes directly with the primary registration CTA, diluting conversion focus. A third 'Sponsorship Opportunities' button also appears in the nav bar area.
findings.recommendation: Differentiate the primary CTA ('Request Your Invite') with the brand accent color (#FF5A36, filled) and reduce the secondary CTA to an outline or ghost button style. Remove or relocate the sponsorship CTA to a dedicated section.
findings.fix_prompt: In the hero CTA row, apply background-color: #FF5A36; color: #ffffff; border: none; to the primary 'Request Your Invite' button, and change the secondary button to background-color: transparent; border: 2px solid #ffffff; color: #ffffff; to visually subordinate it.

findings.issue: The event name 'Corporate Counsel and Compliance Exchange USA' is rendered in a large circular logo lockup but the h1 text treatment is not clearly the most dominant typographic element on screen — the chess imagery and the dark background compete with it visually.
findings.recommendation: Ensure the event name as a text h1 (not just as part of the logo) appears prominently below or beside the logo at the top of the hero with maximum visual weight.
findings.fix_prompt: In the hero section, add an explicit h1 element with text 'Corporate Counsel & Compliance Exchange USA' styled at font-size: 48px; font-weight: 800; color: #ffffff; placed visually above the tagline and dates, separate from the circular logo badge.

findings.issue: The 'Discover All Sponsors' CTA button in the sponsors section uses a color and style that is visually similar to the primary registration CTA, creating hierarchy confusion — a secondary action should not match the primary CTA visually.
findings.recommendation: Style the 'Discover All Sponsors' button as a secondary/outline button (border only, no fill) to keep the registration CTA as the sole filled-accent-color element.
findings.fix_prompt: Change the 'Discover All Sponsors' button class to use background-color: transparent; border: 2px solid #0A2540; color: #0A2540; instead of the primary filled button style.

findings.issue: Button colors observed across the page include blue (#0081ff per CSS --primary-color), yellow (#ffd230 per --secondary-color), and what appears to be a darker navy in some sections. The brand config specifies #FF5A36 as the sole accent for CTAs. None of the visible buttons use the specified accent color.
findings.recommendation: Audit every button on the page and unify all primary CTAs to #FF5A36 background with #FFFFFF text. Secondary/ghost CTAs should use #0A2540 outline only.
findings.fix_prompt: In the CSS, change --primary-color to #FF5A36 and --primary-color-hover to #e04020, then change --secondary-color to #0A2540 and update .btn-primary background-color accordingly. This will propagate the brand accent color to all buttons using those variables.

findings.location: Consistency · Card components — Key Themes cards vs. resource/report cards at bottom of page
findings.issue: The Key Themes cards use a dark background with image overlays and bold title text, while the resource/report cards at the bottom use a light card with image thumbnails and smaller text. Corner radius treatment also differs (themes cards appear rounded, report cards appear square). These are different component designs for what should be a consistent card pattern.
findings.recommendation: Standardize card corner-radius to a single value (e.g. 8px) and define one image overlay approach (either all use gradient overlays or none do) across all card types.
findings.fix_prompt: Set border-radius: 8px on all .card, .theme-card, and .resource-card elements site-wide. For cards with image backgrounds, add a consistent linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(0,0,0,0.1), rgba(0,0,0,0.6)) overlay using a ::after pseudo-element.

findings.issue: Some section headings appear centered (Speakers, Sponsors) while others are left-aligned (Sponsorship Opportunities description text), and at least one uses an underline decoration not seen elsewhere. Alignment is inconsistent without apparent structural reason.
findings.recommendation: Decide on one alignment convention for section headings (recommended: centered for full-width sections, left-aligned for two-column layouts) and apply it consistently.
findings.fix_prompt: Add a global rule: section > .container > [data-component='heading'] h2 { text-align: center; } for all full-width sections, and override with text-align: left only within explicitly two-column layout sections.

findings.location: Responsive integrity · Key Themes cards, mobile (390px)
findings.issue: On mobile, the Key Themes cards appear to stack but retain the chess-board dark background in a way that makes body text inside the cards very difficult to read — the cards appear to overflow or overlap their containing dark section, and card text is not clearly legible against the busy background.
findings.recommendation: On mobile, switch the Key Themes section to a single-column card stack with a solid dark background (#0A2540) per card and white text, removing the imagery overlay entirely at narrow viewports.
findings.fix_prompt: Add a media query: @media (max-width: 768px) { .key-themes-section .card { background-color: #0A2540; background-image: none; color: #ffffff; padding: 24px; margin-bottom: 16px; } } to override the image background on mobile.

findings.location: Responsive integrity · Sponsor logos grid, mobile
findings.issue: On mobile, sponsor logos appear at varying sizes with some appearing very small (barely legible at thumbnail size) and others larger, suggesting logos are not being normalized to a consistent display size in the responsive grid.
findings.recommendation: Set all sponsor logo images to a consistent height (e.g. height: 40px; width: auto; object-fit: contain) within a flex-wrap container on mobile.
findings.fix_prompt: Add @media (max-width: 768px) { .sponsors-grid img { height: 36px; width: auto; max-width: 120px; object-fit: contain; } .sponsors-grid { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: center; gap: 16px; } } to normalize sponsor logo sizes on mobile.

findings.issue: The four stat numbers (75, 22, 194, 27) appear to stack into a 2x2 grid on mobile but the layout looks misaligned in the screenshot — the numbers and labels do not appear to be vertically centered within their cells, and there is uneven spacing between the two rows.
findings.recommendation: Use a CSS grid with grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); gap: 24px; on mobile to enforce equal cell sizes and alignment.
findings.fix_prompt: Add @media (max-width: 768px) { .stats-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); gap: 24px; text-align: center; } .stats-row .stat-item { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; } } to the stylesheet.

findings.issue: The mobile header appears to show a hamburger menu but the logo and sign-in link are very small and cramped against the navigation elements, with inadequate spacing between them.
findings.recommendation: Ensure the mobile header has min-height: 56px and all interactive elements (logo, hamburger) have at least 44px touch target size with 8px minimum padding between them.
findings.fix_prompt: Add @media (max-width: 768px) { .portal-navigation .navbar { min-height: 56px; padding: 8px 16px; } .portal-navigation .navbar-brand img { height: 32px; } .portal-navigation .navbar-toggler { padding: 8px; min-width: 44px; min-height: 44px; } } to the stylesheet.

findings.location: Visual accessibility · Hero section — text over background image, desktop and mobile
findings.issue: The hero places white/light text directly over a busy chess-board photographic background. While there appears to be some darkening, the contrast of the tagline and date text against the mid-tone imagery areas is insufficient — there is no clear full-width scrim or gradient overlay visible behind the body text lines, only behind portions of the layout.
findings.recommendation: Add a linear-gradient overlay (e.g. rgba(10,37,64,0.75) to rgba(10,37,64,0.55)) across the full hero background image to ensure all text meets 4.5:1 contrast against the darkened image.
findings.fix_prompt: In the hero section CSS, change the background to: background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(10,37,64,0.75), rgba(10,37,64,0.65)), url('YOUR_HERO_IMAGE_URL'); background-size: cover; background-position: center; to add a consistent dark scrim over the entire hero.

findings.location: Visual accessibility · Yellow/gold secondary CTA buttons, desktop (hero and elsewhere)
findings.issue: The secondary buttons use --secondary-color: #ffd230 (yellow) with white text. Yellow (#ffd230) against white (#ffffff) text fails WCAG AA contrast (ratio well below 4.5:1). This is also confirmed by the axe-core contrast finding on .btn-primary elements using the current color variables.
findings.recommendation: Change secondary button text to #0A2540 (dark navy) instead of white, which will pass contrast against the yellow background. Alternatively change the button color to a darker hue.
findings.fix_prompt: In the CSS, change .btn-secondary { color: #0A2540 !important; } to replace the white text on yellow buttons with dark text that meets WCAG AA contrast requirements.

findings.location: Visual accessibility · Key Themes cards, desktop — text over image overlays
findings.issue: The four Key Themes cards show text overlaid on photographic images with what appears to be a partial color overlay. The body text inside each card (the paragraph description text below the card title) appears in a small size over imagery where contrast cannot be guaranteed.
findings.recommendation: Add a solid semi-transparent dark panel (background: rgba(10,37,64,0.85)) behind the text content area of each card, separate from the image, to guarantee contrast regardless of image content.
findings.fix_prompt: Add to each theme card's text container: background: rgba(10, 37, 64, 0.85); padding: 16px; border-radius: 0 0 8px 8px; color: #ffffff; to create a legible text band at the bottom of each image card.

findings.issue: Footer link text appears in a small size (visually appears below 12px in the screenshot) against a dark background. While the color may pass contrast, the text size makes it difficult to read for users with moderate visual impairment.
findings.recommendation: Set footer body text and links to a minimum of 12px (brand scale minimum) and ensure all footer links are at least 14px.
findings.fix_prompt: Add footer { font-size: 14px; } footer a { font-size: 14px; color: #ffffff; text-decoration: underline; } to ensure footer text meets minimum legibility standards.

findings.recommendation: Differentiate the primary CTA ('Request Your Invite') with the brand accent color (#FF5A36, filled) and reduce the secondary CTA to an outline or ghost button style. Remove or relocate the sponsorship CTA to a dedicated section.

findings.issue: The event name 'Corporate Counsel and Compliance Exchange USA' is rendered in a large circular logo lockup but the h1 text treatment is not clearly the most dominant typographic element on screen — the chess imagery and the dark background compete with it visually.

findings.fix_prompt: In the hero section, add an explicit h1 element with text 'Corporate Counsel & Compliance Exchange USA' styled at font-size: 48px; font-weight: 800; color: #ffffff; placed visually above the tagline and dates, separate from the circular logo badge.

findings.issue: The 'Discover All Sponsors' CTA button in the sponsors section uses a color and style that is visually similar to the primary registration CTA, creating hierarchy confusion — a secondary action should not match the primary CTA visually.

findings.fix_prompt: Change the 'Discover All Sponsors' button class to use background-color: transparent; border: 2px solid #0A2540; color: #0A2540; instead of the primary filled button style.

findings.issue: Button colors observed across the page include blue (#0081ff per CSS --primary-color), yellow (#ffd230 per --secondary-color), and what appears to be a darker navy in some sections. findings.fix_prompt: In the CSS, change --primary-color to #FF5A36 and --primary-color-hover to #e04020, then change --secondary-color to #0A2540 and update .btn-primary background-color accordingly. This will propagate the brand accent color to all buttons using those variables.

findings.location: Card components — Key Themes cards vs. resource/report cards at bottom of page

Corner radius treatment also differs (themes cards appear rounded, report cards appear square). These are different component designs for what should be a consistent card pattern.
findings.recommendation: Standardize card corner-radius to a single value (e.g. 8px) and define one image overlay approach (either all use gradient overlays or none do) across all card types.
findings.fix_prompt: Set border-radius: 8px on all .card, .theme-card, and .resource-card elements site-wide. For cards with image backgrounds, add a consistent linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(0,0,0,0.1), rgba(0,0,0,0.6)) overlay using a ::after pseudo-element.

findings.issue: Some section headings appear centered (Speakers, Sponsors) while others are left-aligned (Sponsorship Opportunities description text), and at least one uses an underline decoration not seen elsewhere. Alignment is inconsistent without apparent structural reason.
findings.recommendation: Decide on one alignment convention for section headings (recommended: centered for full-width sections, left-aligned for two-column layouts) and apply it consistently.
findings.fix_prompt: Add a global rule: section > .container > [data-component='heading'] h2 { text-align: center; } for all full-width sections, and override with text-align: left only within explicitly two-column layout sections.

findings.issue: On mobile, the Key Themes cards appear to stack but retain the chess-board dark background in a way that makes body text inside the cards very difficult to read — the cards appear to overflow or overlap their containing dark section, and card text is not clearly legible against the busy background.
findings.recommendation: On mobile, switch the Key Themes section to a single-column card stack with a solid dark background (#0A2540) per card and white text, removing the imagery overlay entirely at narrow viewports.
findings.fix_prompt: Add a media query: @media (max-width: 768px) { .key-themes-section .card { background-color: #0A2540; background-image: none; color: #ffffff; padding: 24px; margin-bottom: 16px; } } to override the image background on mobile.

findings.issue: On mobile, sponsor logos appear at varying sizes with some appearing very small (barely legible at thumbnail size) and others larger, suggesting logos are not being normalized to a consistent display size in the responsive grid.

findings.fix_prompt: Add @media (max-width: 768px) { .sponsors-grid img { height: 36px; width: auto; max-width: 120px; object-fit: contain; } .sponsors-grid { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: center; gap: 16px; } } to normalize sponsor logo sizes on mobile.

findings.issue: The four stat numbers (75, 22, 194, 27) appear to stack into a 2x2 grid on mobile but the layout looks misaligned in the screenshot — the numbers and labels do not appear to be vertically centered within their cells, and there is uneven spacing between the two rows.

findings.location: Hero section — text over background image, desktop and mobile
findings.issue: The hero places white/light text directly over a busy chess-board photographic background. findings.fix_prompt: In the hero section CSS, change the background to: background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(10,37,64,0.75), rgba(10,37,64,0.65)), url('YOUR_HERO_IMAGE_URL'); background-size: cover; background-position: center; to add a consistent dark scrim over the entire hero.

findings.location: Yellow/gold secondary CTA buttons, desktop (hero and elsewhere)

findings.fix_prompt: In the CSS, change .btn-secondary { color: #0A2540 !important; } to replace the white text on yellow buttons with dark text that meets WCAG AA contrast requirements.

findings.location: Key Themes cards, desktop — text over image overlays

findings.fix_prompt: Add to each theme card's text container: background: rgba(10, 37, 64, 0.85); padding: 16px; border-radius: 0 0 8px 8px; color: #ffffff; to create a legible text band at the bottom of each image card.

findings.issue: Footer link text appears in a small size (visually appears below 12px in the screenshot) against a dark background. While the color may pass contrast, the text size makes it difficult to read for users with moderate visual impairment.
findings.recommendation: Set footer body text and links to a minimum of 12px (brand scale minimum) and ensure all footer links are at least 14px.
findings.fix_prompt: Add footer { font-size: 14px; } footer a { font-size: 14px; color: #ffffff; text-decoration: underline; } to ensure footer text meets minimum legibility standards.

Keyword coherence is partial: 'legal tech,' 'ALSPs,' and 'corporate governance' appear in copy and metadata, but 'corporate counsel conference,' 'compliance conference USA,' and year/location signals are absent from all visible metadata.
